reason: The text is the CompConsult account name in the greyed-out 2FA Reset row. The probe confirms 2.45:1 on the same span, but the row is inactive: clicking it does nothing, Enter on its arrow button does nothing, and it has no Open Banking button, while the neighbouring rows open a detail panel.
criterionAnalysis: 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component. The row is a selectable control in the master-detail table (Debug, LLC and the others open a detail panel on click), and CompConsult's row is disabled (selectDisabled and hoverDisabled classes; click and Enter on its arrow button changed nothing in the screenshots). 1.4.11 covers non-text contrast of active controls and does not apply to an inactive one. No other A or AA criterion covers the colour of this text. Low-vision users may still struggle to read it, which is a best-practice gap, not an AA failure.

reason: The text is the 2FA Reset badge inside the same greyed-out, inactive CompConsult row. The probe confirms 2.18:1 on the same span, but the row does nothing on click or on Enter, so the badge is text in an inactive component.
criterionAnalysis: 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component, and the badge sits inside the disabled CompConsult row (the _grayedOut wrapper holds the name and the badge together; the row ignores click and Enter on its arrow button). 1.4.11 does not apply to inactive components. The badge explains why the row is unavailable, so a darker colour would help low-vision users, but no A or AA criterion requires it.

reason: Reproduced: the Account column header is a div with a click handler, no tabindex and no role. The focus probe and a full Tab walk never reach it, so keyboard users cannot re-sort by account, which fails 2.1.1. Re-rated low: the table is already sorted by account, all six rows stay readable, and Search by name filters by keyboard.

Reproduced: the Balance column header is a div with a click handler, no tabindex and no role. A click re-sorts the six rows by balance, but the focus probe and a full Tab walk never reach it, which fails 2.1.1. Re-rated low: sorting is a convenience on six rows that are all readable in order, and Search by name filters by keyboard.

The arrow button in the CompConsult row is exposed as button with no name and sits in the Tab order (opacity 0), so it fails 4.1.2. On this disabled row it is also inert: Enter changes nothing, so no task is blocked and the cost is one empty tab stop. Re-rated low.

The arrow button in the Debug, LLC row is exposed as button with no name, has opacity 0 and sits in the Tab order. Enter on it opens the account detail panel (money movement, accounts, graph), and the row click that does the same needs a mouse, so keyboard and screen-reader users must guess that an empty button opens the panel. Possible but hard, so medium; Open Banking is a different, named action and the panel is not the sole route to the account.
